questions.prompt: For scanner events, return package_id, event_type, warehouse_id, copies and spread_minutes (minutes between the first and last copy, rounded to 0 decimals) for every package, event type and warehouse scanned more than once within 15 minutes of its first scan.

questions.title: Sessionize retries and exact boundaries
questions.difficultyWhy: Deduplicate, mark boundaries with a strict comparison, count per day.
questions.prompt: For logical events (one per event_id) that occurred in June 2025, return session_date and sessions per UTC day. A user’s session starts at their first June event or after a gap strictly greater than 30 minutes; a session belongs to the date of its first event.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO events SELECT (SELECT MAX(delivery_id) FROM events) + delivery_id, event_id || '_b', user_id, account_id, session_id, event_name, datetime(occurred_at, '+30 minutes'), datetime(received_at, '+30 minutes') FROM events WHERE occurred_at >= '2025-06-10' AND occurred_at < '2025-06-11' AND delivery_id % 3 = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM events x WHERE x.user_id = events.user_id AND x.occurred_at > events.occurred_at AND x.occurred_at <= datetime(events.occurred_at, '+45 minutes'));

questions.title: Paid conversion by acquisition channel
questions.difficultyWhy: Conversion within a window from signup, by segment.
questions.prompt: For workspaces created before 2025-06-01, return acquisition_channel, workspaces, converted (workspaces with a paid subscription starting within 30 days of creation) and conversion_pct (0–100, 2 decimals).
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE accounts SET acquisition_channel = 'partner' WHERE account_id % 17 = 0;

questions.title: A replay-safe ledger load
questions.difficultyWhy: Idempotent insert from a feed containing duplicates.
questions.prompt: partner_feed contains payroll references, some delivered twice. Load it into partner_ledger (external_ref is the primary key) so that running the same load again adds nothing. Return accounts (distinct account_id), entries and total_cents from partner_ledger.
equivalentSolutions: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO partner_ledger SELECT external_ref, account_id, amount_cents, posted_at FROM partner_feed; SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS accounts, COUNT(*) AS entries, SUM(amount_cents) AS total_cents FROM partner_ledger

stateQueries: SELECT external_ref, account_id, amount_cents, posted_at FROM partner_ledger ORDER BY external_ref

questions.title: Enforce delivery-slot rules
questions.difficultyWhy: Combine CHECK, UNIQUE and FOREIGN KEY constraints.
questions.prompt: Create delivery_slots with slot_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL referencing warehouses(warehouse_id), slot_date TEXT NOT NULL that must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date, capacity INTEGER NOT NULL between 1 and 500, and at most one slot per warehouse and date. Insert (1, 1, '2025-05-01', 120) and (2, 1, '2025-05-02', 80). Return slot_id, warehouse_id, slot_date and capacity.

questions.title: Recover a partially failed transfer
questions.difficultyWhy: Savepoint recovery inside a transaction with state checks.
questions.prompt: In one transaction: post a transfer_out of −25000 cents on account 1 and a matching transfer_in of 25000 on account 3 (both posted at '2025-06-30 12:00:00'); set a savepoint; post a 'fee' of −500 cents on account 1; roll back to the savepoint (the fee was charged in error); commit. Return transaction_type, account_id and amount_cents for ledger entries posted at '2025-06-30 12:00:00'.

stateQueries: SELECT account_id, transaction_type, amount_cents FROM transactions WHERE posted_at = '2025-06-30 12:00:00' ORDER BY account_id, transaction_type

questions.title: Products bought together
questions.difficultyWhy: Self-join on invoice with pair ordering and a count threshold.
questions.prompt: For sale orders in December 2011, return product_a, product_b (stock codes with product_a < product_b) and orders: the number of distinct orders containing both, for pairs bought together on at least 5 orders.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO orders SELECT (SELECT MAX(order_id) FROM orders) + n, 'P9000' || n, 12347, '2011-12-0' || n || ' 10:00:00', 'United Kingdom', 'sale' FROM (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6); INSERT INTO order_items SELECT (SELECT MAX(order_item_id) FROM order_items) + o.order_id * 2 + k.k, o.order_id, k.k, k.code, NULL, 1, 1.0 FROM orders o, (SELECT 1 AS k, 'PET777' AS code UNION ALL SELECT 2, '99999LB') k WHERE o.invoice_no LIKE 'P9000%';

questions.title: Customers who bought from every Home category
questions.difficultyWhy: Relational division with a distinct count against the full set.
questions.prompt: Return customer_id for identified customers who, on 2011 sale orders, bought at least one product from every category in the Home department.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO categories VALUES (18, 'Furniture', 'Home');
equivalentSolutions: SELECT c.customer_id FROM customers c WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM categories k WHERE k.department = 'Home' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.stock_code = i.stock_code WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_type = 'sale' AND o.ordered_at >= '2011-01-01' AND o.ordered_at < '2012-01-01' AND p.category_id = k.category_id))

questions.title: Department audience overlap
questions.difficultyWhy: Reduce to customer-department pairs before self-joining.
questions.prompt: For December 2011 sale orders by identified customers, return department_a, department_b (department_a < department_b) and shared_customers: customers who bought from both departments.
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE products SET category_id = 13 WHERE stock_code IN (SELECT i.stock_code FROM order_items i JOIN orders o USING (order_id) WHERE o.ordered_at >= '2011-12-01' GROUP BY i.stock_code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 5);

questions.title: Parse tracking numbers
questions.difficultyWhy: Normalize, then split a fixed-format code.
questions.prompt: For packages in shipment 1–200, return package_id, carrier_prefix (first two characters), serial (the nine digits after the prefix) and check_letter (the final letter) of the normalized tracking number (trimmed, spaces removed, upper case).
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE packages SET tracking_number = ' ' || lower(tracking_number) WHERE shipment_id BETWEEN 1 AND 200 AND package_id % 4 = 0; UPDATE packages SET tracking_number = 'RT' || printf('%09d', package_id * 7) || 'Z' WHERE shipment_id BETWEEN 1 AND 200 AND package_id % 5 = 0;

questions.title: Normalize invitee emails
questions.difficultyWhy: Text normalization rules including a +tag removal.
questions.prompt: Return invitation_id and normalized_email for invitations whose normalized form differs from the raw invitee_email. Normalize by trimming, lower-casing, and removing any '+tag' before the @.

questions.title: Parse statement amounts into cents
questions.difficultyWhy: Several text formats parsed to exact integers.
questions.prompt: statement_import holds amounts as text: '$1,234.56', '-12.30', '(12.30)' for negatives, ' 12.30 ', '12.3' and 'USD 12.30'. Return line_id and amount_cents as an exact integer for every line.
questions.setupSql:
CREATE TABLE statement_import (line_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id INTEGER NOT NULL, amount_text TEXT);
INSERT INTO statement_import SELECT transaction_id, account_id, CASE transaction_id % 6 WHEN 0 THEN printf('$%,.2f', amount_cents / 100.0) WHEN 1 THEN printf('%.2f', amount_cents / 100.0) WHEN 2 THEN CASE WHEN amount_cents < 0 THEN printf('(%.2f)', -amount_cents / 100.0) ELSE printf('%.2f', amount_cents / 100.0) END WHEN 3 THEN printf(' %.2f ', amount_cents / 100.0) WHEN 4 THEN printf('%.1f', amount_cents / 100.0) ELSE printf('USD %.2f', amount_cents / 100.0) END FROM transactions WHERE status = 'posted' AND account_id BETWEEN 1 AND 40 AND transaction_type <> 'interest';
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE statement_import SET amount_text = '$9,999.99' WHERE line_id % 11 = 0; UPDATE statement_import SET amount_text = '(0.29)' WHERE line_id % 13 = 0;

questions.title: Upgrade review 1: the daily pricing audience
questions.difficultyWhy: Daily distinct counts on deduplicated events.
questions.prompt: The product team is reviewing self-serve upgrades in Q2 2025. Return day, pricing_viewers (distinct users with a pricing_viewed event that day) and pricing_views (logical pricing_viewed events) for every day in April–June 2025 with at least one view.

questions.title: Upgrade review 2: where the funnel drops

questions.title: Upgrade review 3: time from checkout to subscription
questions.difficultyWhy: Pair each checkout with its subscription, then a percentile.
questions.prompt: For Q2 2025 checkouts that were followed by a subscription within 24 hours, measure minutes from checkout to the first such subscription. Return conversions, avg_minutes and p90_minutes (the smallest delay at or above the 90th percentile by position: row ceil(0.9 × n)), each rounded to 1 decimal.

questions.title: Upgrade review 4: abandoned checkouts that came back
questions.difficultyWhy: Abandonment and later recovery with two windows.
questions.prompt: For Q2 2025 checkouts with no subscription within 24 hours, return abandoned (logical checkout events), recovered_14d (those whose workspace started a subscription between 24 hours and 14 days after the checkout) and recovery_pct (0–100, 2 decimals).

questions.title: Upgrade review 5: which channels to fix first
questions.difficultyWhy: Segment the funnel, then rank segments by lost conversions.
questions.prompt: For Q2 2025 logical checkouts, return acquisition_channel (of the workspace), checkouts, converted (subscription within 24 hours), lost (checkouts − converted) and priority: RANK by lost descending.

questions.title: Predict: patients with and without missed appointments
questions.difficultyWhy: A LEFT JOIN with unmatched and repeated matches.
questions.prompt: Predict every row returned when the six sample patients are LEFT JOINed to their cancelled or missed appointments.
questions.setupSql: CREATE VIEW patient_sample AS SELECT patient_id, insurance_type FROM patients WHERE patient_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6; CREATE VIEW missed_appointments AS SELECT appointment_id, patient_id, status FROM appointments WHERE patient_id BETWEEN 1 AND 6 AND status IN ('cancelled', 'no_show');

questions.title: Predict: unknown passenger counts in a filter

questions.prompt: Predict the trips returned by a filter for passenger counts other than 1.

questions.title: Predict: count rows or known values?
questions.difficultyWhy: Three COUNT forms over NULLs and duplicates.
questions.prompt: Predict the single row of counts over the sample products.
questions.setupSql: CREATE VIEW product_sample AS SELECT stock_code, description, category_id, list_price FROM products WHERE stock_code BETWEEN '21017' AND '21026';

questions.title: Predict: positions and shared ranks
questions.difficultyWhy: RANK, DENSE_RANK and ROW_NUMBER over ties.
questions.prompt: Predict the three ranking columns for the sample of Seattle hitters.

questions.title: Predict: a frame that includes peers
questions.difficultyWhy: The default RANGE frame includes rows with equal ORDER BY values.
questions.prompt: Predict the running total ordered by posting date (not time) for account 1 in late January.

questions.title: Predict: the previous leg of the same aircraft
questions.difficultyWhy: LAG within partitions, NULL at each partition start.
questions.prompt: Predict previous_destination for each sample flight.

questions.title: Debug: find measurements with no value
questions.prompt: The query should return observation_id and code for observations whose value was not obtained, but it returns nothing. Fix it.

questions.title: Debug: keep carriers without next-day shipments

questions.prompt: Return carrier_id, carrier_name and next_day_shipments (service_level_id 4) for every carrier, 0 when none. The current query drops carriers with no next-day shipments.

questions.title: Debug: count zero projects correctly

questions.prompt: Return account_id and projects for every workspace created in June 2025. Workspaces without projects currently show 1. Fix the count.

questions.title: Debug: the second-best win total
questions.difficultyWhy: ROW_NUMBER versus DENSE_RANK for distinct values.

questions.title: Debug: February flights at the boundary

questions.title: Debug: each account’s last posted amount
questions.difficultyWhy: LAST_VALUE needs an explicit full frame.
questions.prompt: For posted entries on accounts 1–30, return transaction_id, account_id and last_amount: the account’s final posted amount (by posted_at, transaction_id). The query returns each row’s own amount. Fix it.

questions.title: Grid review 1: regional demand on a peak day
questions.difficultyWhy: Join to a dimension and aggregate a UTC day.

questions.prompt: For January 2024, return observation_date, central_park, jfk and laguardia: each station’s tmax_c that day (NULL when not reported).

questions.difficultyWhy: Merge overlapping work orders before measuring downtime.
questions.prompt: For completed maintenance, merge overlapping [started_at, completed_at) jobs per device. Return device_id, window_start, window_end, jobs and downtime_hours (window length in hours, 1 decimal).
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO maintenance (maintenance_id, device_id, maintenance_type, technician, started_at, completed_at, cost) SELECT 900000 + maintenance_id, device_id, 'repair', 'probe', datetime(started_at, '-30 minutes'), datetime(completed_at, '+3 days'), 100 FROM maintenance WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL AND maintenance_id % 9 = 0; INSERT INTO maintenance (maintenance_id, device_id, maintenance_type, technician, started_at, completed_at, cost) SELECT 950000 + maintenance_id, device_id, 'calibration', 'probe', datetime(started_at, '+1 day'), datetime(started_at, '+1 day', '+1 hour'), 50 FROM maintenance WHERE completed_at IS NOT NULL AND maintenance_id % 9 = 0;

questions.title: Continuous medication coverage
questions.difficultyWhy: Merge date ranges where adjacent days also count as continuous.
questions.prompt: For patients 1–200, merge each patient’s fills of the same medication_name into continuous coverage periods: a fill continues the period when its start_date is no later than the day after the latest stop_date so far. Return patient_id, medication_name, covered_from, covered_to and fills.

questions.title: When did devices go silent?
questions.difficultyWhy: Gap detection relative to each device’s own reporting interval.
questions.prompt: Return device_id, last_seen, next_seen and silent_minutes for every gap between consecutive readings that is longer than three times the device’s reporting_interval_minutes.

questions.title: Three late legs in a row
questions.difficultyWhy: Consecutive-event streaks within an aircraft’s day.
questions.prompt: For January 2025, consider each aircraft’s operated (not cancelled, not diverted) flights per flight_date in scheduled order. Return tail_number, flight_date, first_departure and late_legs for every run of at least 3 consecutive flights arriving more than 15 minutes late.
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE flights SET arrival_delay = 0 WHERE flight_id IN (SELECT flight_id FROM flights WHERE flight_date = '2025-01-10' AND arrival_delay > 15 AND cancelled = 0 AND diverted = 0 LIMIT 40); UPDATE flights SET arrival_delay = 45 WHERE flight_date = '2025-01-20' AND tail_number IN (SELECT tail_number FROM flights WHERE flight_date = '2025-01-20' AND cancelled = 0 GROUP BY tail_number HAVING COUNT(*) >= 4 LIMIT 5) AND cancelled = 0 AND diverted = 0;

questions.title: Back-to-back failed deliveries
questions.difficultyWhy: Compare each attempt with the one before it.
questions.prompt: Return package_id, attempt_number, previous_outcome and outcome for every attempt that failed (outcome other than 'delivered') directly after a failed attempt.
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE delivery_attempts SET outcome = 'recipient_absent' WHERE attempt_id IN (SELECT a.attempt_id FROM delivery_attempts a JOIN delivery_attempts p ON p.package_id = a.package_id AND p.attempt_number = a.attempt_number - 1 AND p.outcome <> 'delivered' WHERE a.outcome = 'delivered' LIMIT 30);

questions.title: Each patient’s latest systolic reading
questions.difficultyWhy: A correlated subquery chooses the latest row, not the largest value.
questions.prompt: For patients 1–400 with at least one known systolic reading (code BP_SYS), return patient_id, observed_at and value of the latest one (ties by highest observation_id).
equivalentSolutions: SELECT patient_id, observed_at, value FROM (SELECT patient_id, observed_at, value, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY patient_id ORDER BY observed_at DESC, observation_id DESC) AS rn FROM observations WHERE code = 'BP_SYS' AND value IS NOT NULL AND patient_id BETWEEN 1 AND 400) WHERE rn = 1

questions.title: Purchases far above a card’s norm
questions.difficultyWhy: Compare each row with an aggregate of its own group.
questions.prompt: Return authorization_id, card_id, amount and card_avg (the card’s average approved amount, 2 decimals) for approved authorizations more than three times their card’s average approved amount.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT a.authorization_id, a.card_id, a.amount, ROUND((SELECT AVG(b.amount) FROM authorizations b WHERE b.card_id = a.card_id AND b.status = 'approved'), 2) AS card_avg FROM authorizations a WHERE a.status = 'approved' AND a.amount > 3 * (SELECT AVG(b.amount) FROM authorizations b WHERE b.card_id = a.card_id AND b.status = 'approved')

questions.title: Reviewers who cover every team repository
questions.difficultyWhy: Relational division with a double NOT EXISTS.
questions.prompt: Return developer_id and team_id for developers whose team owns at least two active (unarchived) repositories and who reviewed at least one pull request in every one of them.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT d.developer_id, d.team_id FROM developers d JOIN repositories r ON r.owning_team_id = d.team_id AND r.archived_at IS NULL LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT p.repository_id, v.reviewer_id FROM pull_requests p JOIN reviews v ON v.pull_request_id = p.pull_request_id) x ON x.repository_id = r.repository_id AND x.reviewer_id = d.developer_id GROUP BY d.developer_id, d.team_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 AND COUNT(x.reviewer_id) = COUNT(*)

questions.title: Headcount of each team tree
questions.difficultyWhy: Carry the root through a recursive walk, then aggregate.
questions.prompt: For every top-level team (no parent), return team_id, subteams (descendant teams at any depth) and developers (current developers — left_at NULL — in the team or any descendant).
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE teams SET parent_team_id = (SELECT MIN(team_id) FROM teams c WHERE c.parent_team_id IS NOT NULL AND c.organization_id = teams.organization_id AND c.team_id <> teams.team_id) WHERE team_id IN (SELECT MAX(team_id) FROM teams WHERE parent_team_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY organization_id LIMIT 6);

questions.title: Direct and total reports
questions.difficultyWhy: Direct versus transitive counts from one recursive expansion.
questions.prompt: For managers with at least 10 total reports, return manager_id, direct_reports and total_reports (everyone below them at any depth).

questions.title: A histogram of daily highs
questions.difficultyWhy: Floor-based buckets that are correct below zero.
questions.prompt: For 2024, bin every known tmax_c into 5 °C buckets [bucket_start, bucket_start + 5). Return bucket_start and days.
equivalentSolutions: SELECT CAST(tmax_c / 5.0 AS INTEGER) * 5 - CASE WHEN tmax_c < 0 AND tmax_c / 5.0 <> CAST(tmax_c / 5.0 AS INTEGER) THEN 5 ELSE 0 END AS bucket_start, COUNT(*) AS days FROM daily_weather WHERE tmax_c IS NOT NULL AND observation_date >= '2024-01-01' AND observation_date < '2025-01-01' GROUP BY bucket_start

questions.title: How far do taxi trips go?
questions.difficultyWhy: Capped buckets with a share of the total.
questions.prompt: For trips with a positive trip_distance_miles, return bucket (whole miles 0–9, with 10 or more labelled 10) , trips and pct_of_trips (2 decimals).

questions.title: Median and 90th-percentile arrival delay
questions.prompt: For each airline, among flights with a known arrival_delay, return airline_code, p50 and p90: the nearest-rank percentile (the value at position ⌈p × n⌉ in ascending order).

questions.title: Fork families
questions.difficultyWhy: Walk a graph of forks across generations.
questions.prompt: For original repositories (not forks) that have at least one fork, return repository_id, forks (descendants at any generation) and generations (deepest level).
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO repositories (repository_id, organization_id, owning_team_id, repo_name, primary_language, visibility, created_at, archived_at, forked_from_repository_id) SELECT 90000 + repository_id, organization_id, owning_team_id, repo_name || '-fork2', primary_language, visibility, '2025-06-01 00:00:00', NULL, repository_id FROM repositories WHERE forked_from_repository_id IS NOT NULL;

questions.title: Who is within two reviews?
questions.difficultyWhy: Bounded graph traversal with the shortest distance per node.
questions.prompt: Treat “reviewer reviewed a pull request by author” as an edge reviewer → author. Starting from developer 7, return developer_id and steps (the fewest edges, 1 or 2) for everyone reachable within two steps, excluding developer 7.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO reviews (review_id, pull_request_id, reviewer_id, submitted_at, state) SELECT 900000 + pull_request_id, pull_request_id, 7, datetime(created_at, '+1 day'), 'approved' FROM pull_requests WHERE pull_request_id % 997 = 0 AND author_id <> 7;

questions.title: Developers who review each other
questions.difficultyWhy: Symmetric pairs by joining a relationship to its reverse.
questions.prompt: Return developer_a, developer_b (developer_a < developer_b), a_reviewed_b and b_reviewed_a (review counts each way) for pairs who have each reviewed the other at least 3 times.

questions.title: Routes flown in one direction only
questions.difficultyWhy: An anti-join against the reversed relationship.
questions.prompt: Return origin and destination for routes whose reverse (destination → origin) does not exist in routes.
questions.extraMutation: DELETE FROM routes WHERE route_id IN (SELECT r.route_id FROM routes r JOIN routes b ON b.origin = r.destination AND b.destination = r.origin WHERE r.origin < r.destination LIMIT 25);
equivalentSolutions: SELECT r.origin, r.destination FROM routes r LEFT JOIN routes b ON b.origin = r.destination AND b.destination = r.origin WHERE b.route_id IS NULL

questions.title: Retried authorization requests
questions.difficultyWhy: Deduplicate by business key, keeping the final attempt, before aggregating.
questions.prompt: Per merchant, return merchant_id, attempts (rows), requests (distinct request_key) and approved_amount: the sum of amount over requests whose final attempt (latest requested_at, then highest authorization_id) was approved, rounded to 2. Only merchants with at least one retried request.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO authorizations (authorization_id, request_key, card_id, merchant_id, requested_at, amount, currency, channel, status, decline_reason) SELECT 900000 + authorization_id, request_key, card_id, merchant_id, datetime(requested_at, '+20 seconds'), amount, currency, channel, 'approved', NULL FROM authorizations WHERE status = 'approved' AND authorization_id % 50 = 0;

questions.title: Encounters that overlap in time
questions.difficultyWhy: Interval overlap test in a self-join, each pair once.
questions.prompt: Return patient_id, first_encounter, second_encounter (first_encounter < second_encounter) and overlap_minutes for every pair of the same patient’s encounters whose [start_at, end_at) intervals overlap.
questions.extraMutation: UPDATE encounters SET start_at = datetime(start_at, '-2 days') WHERE encounter_id IN (SELECT b.encounter_id FROM encounters a JOIN encounters b ON b.patient_id = a.patient_id AND a.encounter_id < b.encounter_id AND a.start_at < b.end_at AND b.start_at < a.end_at LIMIT 20); UPDATE encounters SET end_at = datetime(end_at, '+2 days') WHERE encounter_class = 'inpatient' AND encounter_id % 5 = 0;

questions.title: Predict: payments after joining line items
questions.difficultyWhy: Two one-to-many joins multiply each other.
questions.prompt: Predict line_rows and paid_total for the two sample orders when items and payments are joined together.
questions.setupSql: CREATE VIEW order_sample AS SELECT order_id, invoice_no FROM orders WHERE order_id IN (211, 275); CREATE VIEW item_sample AS SELECT order_id, stock_code, quantity, unit_price FROM order_items WHERE order_id IN (211, 275); CREATE VIEW payment_sample AS SELECT payment_id, order_id, amount FROM payments WHERE order_id IN (211, 275);

questions.title: Debug: redelivered events
questions.difficultyWhy: At-least-once delivery creates duplicate rows for one event.
questions.prompt: Return day and events (distinct product events that occurred that day) for June 2025. The pipeline redelivers some events under a new delivery_id; the query counts deliveries. Fix it.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO events (delivery_id, event_id, user_id, account_id, session_id, event_name, occurred_at, received_at) SELECT 10000000 + delivery_id, event_id, user_id, account_id, session_id, event_name, occurred_at, datetime(received_at, '+1 hour') FROM events WHERE occurred_at >= '2025-06-01' AND occurred_at < '2025-07-01' AND delivery_id % 11 = 0;

questions.title: Predict: which trips are in January?
questions.difficultyWhy: BETWEEN with a date-only upper bound on timestamps.
questions.prompt: Predict both flags for each sample trip around midnight on 31 January.
questions.setupSql: CREATE VIEW midnight_sample AS SELECT trip_id, pickup_at FROM trips WHERE trip_id BETWEEN 38460 AND 38463 OR trip_id BETWEEN 40011 AND 40014;

questions.title: Debug: sessions and events per workspace
questions.difficultyWhy: Aggregate each child table to the target grain before joining.
questions.prompt: For workspaces 1–40, return account_id, sessions and events (distinct event_id) started or occurring in March 2024, 0 when none. The current query multiplies sessions by events. Fix it.
questions.extraMutation: INSERT INTO sessions (session_id, user_id, started_at, ended_at, device) SELECT 900000 + session_id, user_id, datetime(started_at, '+1 hour'), datetime(ended_at, '+1 hour'), device FROM sessions WHERE started_at >= '2024-03-01' AND started_at < '2024-03-29' AND session_id % 2 = 0 AND user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM users WHERE account_id BETWEEN 1 AND 40);
